0.0.n: This is the name of a Japanese discount store chain.

0.1.n: Links the store name to the product, showing where it comes from.

0.2.n: Combines with トレー to describe the tray's intended use.

0.3.n: A borrowed English word written in katakana.

0.4.n: Politely identifies the item; the subject, meaning this, is left unstated.

1.0.n: Names the room whose wall is being discussed.

1.1.n: Links キッチン to 壁, identifying which wall.

1.2.n: This noun is followed by など, so walls are one example of possible locations.

1.3.n: Shows that walls are examples, not the only possible locations.

1.4.n: Marks the location where the storage space can be created.

1.5.n: Refers to cooking ingredients such as salt, spices, and sauces.

1.6.n: Shows that seasonings are examples of what you can store.

1.7.n: Marks seasonings and similar things as what you place.

1.8.n: The plain form of the verb describes what the following スペース is for.

1.9.n: The phrase before it describes its purpose: somewhere to put seasonings.

1.10.n: Marks スペース as what the item lets you create.

1.11.n: The ability form of 作る describes what the following アイテム enables you to do.

1.12.n: The preceding description modifies this noun; the sentence ends without です in a compact product-description style.

2.0.n: Describes how frequently the seasonings are used, rather than how well they are used.

2.1.n: The plain form directly describes 調味料: seasonings you use often.

2.2.n: Modified by よく使う, specifying the ones used frequently.

2.3.n: Extends the list beyond seasonings without naming every possible item.

2.4.n: Marks seasonings and similar things as what you gather together.

2.5.n: The て-form of まとめる connects organizing the items with making them easy to retrieve.

2.7.n: 調理 means cooking; adding 中 makes 調理中 mean during that activity.

2.8.n: Highlights that easy access is possible during cooking too.

2.9.n: Suggests a swift, easy movement; the small ッ gives the expression a brisk feel.

2.10.n: The ability form of 取り出す refers to retrieving the stored items.

2.11.n: Follows the ability form and joins に to express the desired result.

2.12.n: Joins よう to できます, linking the desired result to making it possible.

2.13.n: The polite form of できる completes ようにできます, expressing that you can arrange things for this result.

0.tip: Japanese often leaves out the subject when the item being shown is obvious.

1.lit: An item that can create space on kitchen walls and similar places to put seasonings and similar things.
1.tip: Everything before アイテム describes the item; Japanese places these descriptions before the noun.

2.lit: Gather frequently used seasonings and similar things together, and can make it so you can retrieve them quickly even while cooking.
2.tip: An ability verb followed by ようにできます means you can arrange things so that action becomes possible.
